The test image is a newspaper article (Dallas Morning News, March 4, 2001) with the headline "Corn toxin examined in border birth defects." The caption on the right side reads: **"Fumonisin, a toxin produced by a corn mold, may be connected to the '91 outbreak."** There is a photo of corn on the right side of the article.

Key observations:
- The article is explicitly about **fumonisin**, a mycotoxin produced by *Fusarium* fungi (primarily *F. verticillioides*)
- The image context directly implicates Fusarium ear rot as the source disease
- Fumonisin is the signature toxin of Fusarium ear rot in corn
- The Fusarium class description mentions "white to pink or salmon-colored cottony mold on kernels" — consistent with the corn shown

This maps clearly to **Fusarium** ear rot.
